title: Encouraging Locally Incorporated Tech Companies to Choose Singapore Exchange over Foreign Stock Markets for IPOs
what_it_is: Encouraging Locally Incorporated Tech Companies to Choose Singapore Exchange over Foreign Stock Markets for IPOs

sections.label: Equities market support initiatives
sections.summary: Government agencies and SGX established initiatives including the Anchor Fund @ 65, EDBI Growth IPO Fund, enhanced MAS grants and a Thailand-Singapore DR Connect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, we have shared in this House, most recently in November 2022, the initiatives that Government agencies and the Singapore Exchange (SGX) have established in recent years to support the attractiveness of our equities market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We have set up the S$1.5 billion Anchor Fund @ 65, which is a co-investment fund by the Government and Temasek, and the S$500 million EDBI Growth IPO Fund, to invest in high-growth enterprises at the late stage or at IPO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has enhanced its grant scheme to defray listing costs and develop Singapore’s equity research ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In May this year, to expand access and connectivity to regional capital markets, SGX launched a Thailand-Singapore Depository Receipt or DR Connect, to broaden access to capital and to markets.

sections.label: SME financing and Catalist
sections.summary: SGX's Catalist second board has over 200 SMEs listed, and MAS raised the grant cap from S$200,000 to S$300,000 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: One way is to make sure we have good sources of SME financing available to meet our SMEs' needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: And apart from a well-developed banking system that provides a range of financing options for our SMEs, SGX has Catalist, a second board that caters to the fundraising needs of growth-stage companies or enterprises and currently has over 200 SMEs listed on it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In 2021, MAS increased the grant cap under this scheme from S$200,000 to S$300,000, to further help SMEs who choose to list on Catalist, to alleviate their listing costs.

sections.label: Data not collected
sections.summary: The Government does not collect that data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To the first question, we do not collect that data.

sections.label: Delistings and SGX listings
sections.summary: Since 2014 delistings have surpassed IPOs, and as of April 2023 SGX had 650 listed companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since 2014, there has been a trend where the number of delistings has surpassed the number of IPOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As of April 2023, the total number of listed companies on SGX stood at 650.

sections.label: Limits on encouraging listings
sections.summary: The speaker says there is a limit to what can be done to encourage listings and Singapore takes a different approach from Indonesia's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier on also, I think it is important for us to try to play a part but there is also a limit to what we can do to encourage listings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I do not have an answer, but I think the short answer to the Member's first question is that we just take a very different approach to Indonesia's.
